title: Longitudinal observational study of geriatric intensive care patients
summary:
Older adults often need intensive care after major surgery. Recovery can vary widely: some patients regain their health and quality of life quickly, while others experience lasting problems with mobility, memory, or mood. We want to understand these differences more clearly.

In this study, we follow patients aged 60 years and older who are scheduled for elective surgery with a planned ICU stay. Before surgery, we assess health, mobility, memory, and mood, and we take a small blood sample and a skin measurement. After three and six months, we conduct short telephone interviews about quality of life, daily functioning, and hospital readmissions. Our goal is to identify factors that promote good recovery and to develop better ways of supporting older patients after surgery and intensive care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled elective surgery

Planned postoperative ICU stay ≥ 24 hours

Capacity to provide informed consent (no acute delirium, no severe dementia)

Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal to participate

Acute delirium at the time of consent

Severe dementia precluding informed consent and valid assessment (according to prior clinical diagnosis/documentation)
